questions.question: Which of the following quality marks are NOT correctly matched?
questions.solution:
Option **4** is correct:

__
 
• **ISI** stands for the **Indian Standards Institute**.
 
• Indian Standards Institute, a body set up when India gained Independence to create **standards needed for orderly commercial growth and maintaining quality in industrial production.__**

• But the term **“ISI mark"** continues to be used to mean that a certain product conforms to the quality standards set up by the government.

• The process of certifying the purity of jewellery is called **hallmarking**.

questions.question: Which of the following is also called the First Law of Thermodynamics?
questions.solution:
the correct answer is the __**Law of Conservation of Energy.**__

__
 
• **The Law of Conservation of Energy**__ is also called the **first law of Thermodynamics.**
 
• The first law of thermodynamics states that the energy of the universe remains the same.
 
• Though it may be exchanged between the system and the surround
ings, it can’t be created or destroyed.
 
• The law basically relates to the changes in energy states due to work and heat transfer.
 
• The total energy of a system remains conserved.
 
• The equation for the first law of thermodynamics is given as:
 
 
• **ΔU = q + W**
 
• Where,
 
• ΔU = change in internal energy of the system.
 
• q = algebraic sum of heat transfer between system and surroundings.
 
• W = work interaction of the system with its surroundings

questions.question: Ozone gas is present in which layer of atmosphere?
questions.solution:
Option **2** s correct:

__
 
• **The stratosphere** is where you find the very important ozone layer__.
 
• **The stratosphere** is a layer of Earth’s atmosphere.
 
• The stratosphere is located above the troposphere and below the mesosphere.
 
• **“Strat” means layer**, this layer of our atmosphere has its own set of layers.
 
• There are no storms or turbulence here to mix up the air, so cold, heavy air is at the bottom and warm, light air is at the top.
 
• This layer is 22 miles (35 kilometers) thick.
 
• The ozone layer helps protect us from **ultraviolet radiation (UV)** from the sun.
 
• In fact, the ozone layer absorbs most of the UV radiation the sun sends to us.
 
• Life as we know it wouldn’t be possible without this layer of protection.

questions.question: Which of the following adjectives is NOT a part of the Preamble?
questions.solution:
Option **2** is correct:

__
 
• Liberty, Secular, Sovereign is a part of Preamble, but **Tolerant** __is not a part of Preamble.
 
• The preamble has been amended only once so far.
 
• On **18 December 1976**, during the Emergency in India, the Indira Gandhi government pushed through several changes in the **42nd Amendment of the constitution**.
 
• In this amendment, the words **"socialist"** and **"secular"** were added between the words **"Sovereign"** and **"democratic"** and the words** "unity of the Nation"** were changed to **"unity and integrity of the Nation"**.
 
• The **Preamble** of the Indian Constitution has been adopted on **26 November 1949**.
 
• It is a brief introductory statement setting out guidelines that guide the people of the nation and the principles of the Constitution, indicating the source and meaning of the document.
 
• It adopted by Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 but came into action on **26 January 1950(Republic Day of India)**.
 
• In the Berubari case presidential reference, the Supreme Court of India originally stated that the preamble is not an integral part of the Indian constitution.
 
• The Preamble of Indian Constitution based on Objectives Resolution.

questions.question: Who renounced his Knighthood against the Jallianwala Bagh atrocity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rabindranath Tagore**__.

__
 
• Rabindranath Tagore__ renounced his Knighthood against the Jallianwala Bagh atrocity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre, also known as the Amritsar massacre, took place on 13 April 1919 in Jallianwala Bagh, Punjab.

 
 
• People gathered at Jallianwala Bagh to celebrate the festival of Baisakhi and to protest against the arrest of two leaders, Satyapal and Saifuddin Kitchlew.
 
• General Dyer with his troops, blocked all exits of the bagh and opened fire on the innocent and unarmed people.
 
• Gandhiji returned his Kaiser-i-Hind medal to mark his protest.
 
• Hunter Commission was set up to enquire into the massacre.
 
• **“Gitanjali”** is a collection of poems by the Bengali poet Rabindranath Tagore.
 
• Tagore received the Nobel Prize for Literature for the book in the year 1913 was the first Indian to get Nobel Prize in literature.
 
 
• He was also the first Asian to win the Nobel Prize.
 
• The national anthem of India is **"Jana Gana Mana"** which was written by the Nobel laureate **Rabindranath Tagore**.
